turns.prompt_text: is there a way to check the water heater to see how much hot water there is
turns.response_html:
Standard water heaters do not have a built-in "fuel gauge," but you can check levels using these methods:

1. Smart Controllers (Best for Accuracy)

You can install a smart water heater controller (like Aquanta or Hilo). These devices use sensors on the outside of the tank to track temperature profiles and provide a real-time "hot water available" percentage via a smartphone app.

2. Manual Temperature Check

Since hot water rises, you can feel the side of the tank (if it isn't heavily insulated) or the outlet pipes.

  • The Top: Should always be the hottest.
  • The Middle/Bottom: If the bottom half of the tank feels cool to the touch, you have likely used more than 50% of your hot water reserve.

3. External Temperature Sensors

For a DIY approach, you can strap digital thermocouple sensors to the top, middle, and bottom of the tank under the insulation. When the bottom sensor temperature drops, it indicates cold water has entered and "pushed" the remaining hot water to the top.

4. Estimating by Use

You can estimate remaining capacity based on your tank's First Hour Rating (FHR), found on the yellow EnergyGuide label.

  • Average Shower: Uses ~20 gallons.
  • Dishwasher: Uses ~6 gallons. If you have a 40-gallon tank and two people just showered, you are likely near empty.
